title: Ankhorage GitHub Auth
summary: Implements the provider-neutral Ankhorage authentication port with GitHub App and OAuth App authorization.
purpose: Provide a standalone server-side GitHub browser-authorization adapter with explicit host-owned session and one-time attempt persistence.
responsibilities: Start and complete GitHub App or OAuth App browser authorization flows.
Exchange and refresh GitHub user tokens while preserving the authenticated user identity.
Normalize GitHub and session failures into provider-neutral authentication results.
boundaries: Does not own repository discovery, GitHub API rate-limit handling, or repository materialization.
Does not own durable sessions or authorization-attempt storage.
Does not implement password, registration, password-reset, or OTP authentication.
audience: Server applications that authenticate GitHub users through the Ankhorage authentication port.
Hosts that provide secure session and atomic one-time attempt persistence.
useCases: Authenticate a user through a GitHub App user-authorization flow.
Authenticate a user through a classic GitHub OAuth App flow.
Read, refresh, and clear a host-persisted GitHub session.

architecture.role: Provider adapter at the GitHub OAuth boundary for the published AuthPort.
invariants: Client secrets and user tokens remain on the server-side provider boundary.
Redirect URIs are exact allowlisted HTTPS URLs.
Authorization attempts are durable, short-lived, and atomically consumed once.

configuration: Requires an explicit GitHub App or OAuth App mode, client credentials, HTTPS redirect allowlist, and host-provided stores.
security: Tokens and client secrets are never placed in browser URLs, diagnostics, generated documentation, or shared process-global storage.
Authorization callbacks use one-time state bound to an explicitly registered redirect URI.
limitations: The generic AuthPort credential and OTP operations return unsupported-operation results.
